title: Name the behaviour, not the child
statement: When a learner games a task, name the behaviour, never the learner, and explain any penalty at the end with the way back, never as a live scold.
example: A whole set answered in under 10 seconds costs one point, but the running counter never goes negative while the child is still working.
detail: A Grade 3 reading sample's points rubric sets how gaming is shown to a child: the speed-click message names the behaviour, not the child, saying the set was answered faster than anyone can read it, that points are for thinking time and that reading it again brings the points straight back, with no shaming word. The running counter never goes negative while the child is still working, because the penalty is something to explain at the end, not a live scold, and on the end card the negative is shown with its explanation directly beneath it. A total of zero says so kindly, with the way to earn points in the same breath. These are design decisions in one sample, with no outcome measured.

evidence.quote: The speed-click message names the behaviour, not the child.
The running counter never goes negative while the child is still working.
